name: Aider
description: Tier B capture: overrides Aider's $SHELL so every command Aider runs on the pexpect (TTY) code path is bracketed with command_start / command_end events on RedLog's timeline.
author: your-handle

capture.name: Aider (SHELL wrapper)
capture.description: Wraps every shell command Aider spawns (pexpect / TTY code path) so it lands in the RedLog timeline as an agent event.

manualSteps.label: Point $SHELL at the wrapper. Aider's run_cmd() reads os.environ['SHELL'] and invokes it as `$SHELL -i -c '<command>'` on the pexpect (TTY) code path.
Launch Aider through the wrapper for a single session (recommended — doesn't touch your login shell)
OR persist across sessions by exporting SHELL in your shell rc. WARNING: this changes the default shell for every process you launch from that terminal, not just Aider.
Smoke-test: this should print 'hello' AND create a command_start/command_end pair on the RedLog timeline

NOTE — Aider only routes commands through $SHELL on the pexpect (interactive TTY) code path. Non-TTY runs and Windows fall back to subprocess.Popen(shell=True), which on POSIX always uses /bin/sh regardless of $SHELL — those commands will NOT be captured. See https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider/blob/main/aider/run_cmd.py.
